coverage_of_risk.rationale: The app contains zero tests; the riskiest logic (data transformation, filtering, pagination, URL state, sorting) is entirely unguarded once the external acceptance suite is removed.

evidence: app/src/routes/index.tsx:38-43 — popstate sync reads location.url.href captured at render; raw history.pushState at lines 104, 135 never updates it, so back/forward can desync filters from the URL — nothing would catch this

evidence: app/ — no test files, so no noise either
signal_to_noise.rationale: No tests: per the rubric this scores 3; there is no padding because there is nothing at all.

findings.issue: No test infrastructure whatsoever: no runner in devDependencies, no test script, no spec files; ~300 lines of data-transformation logic in lib/api.ts plus URL-state and sorting logic are completely unguarded once the external acceptance suite is gone.
findings.suggestion: Add Vitest (Qwik's recommended runner) with unit tests for the pure helpers in lib/format.ts and lib/api.ts (humanize, dexNumber, idFromUrl, englishName, latestFlavor, cardsFromPokemonRefs, entriesByMethod table construction) and a component test for MoveTable sorting/aria-sort against fixture rows.

findings.issue: The popstate sync handler reads location.url.href from useLocation, which was captured at render time and is never updated because the filters/pagination use raw window.history.pushState/replaceState (lines 104, 135, 181) instead of Qwik City's navigate — after back/forward the controls can show stale filter state. No test exercises back/forward.
findings.suggestion: Read window.location.href inside the popstate handler instead of the captured location.url, and add a Playwright test for browser back/forward syncing the URL with the rendered list.

findings.issue: fetchJson caches 404 responses as null forever; the spec treats the API as live data that can change, so a resource that was missing once is permanently not-found for the server process lifetime, and this behaviour is untested.
findings.suggestion: Cache only successful responses (delete 404-null entries like thrown errors are deleted at lines 94-96), or add a TTL; cover with a unit test using a mock fetch that 404s then succeeds.

findings.issue: The level-up dedup keeps only the minimum level_learned_at per move per game, an unverified business rule; a move learnable at multiple levels (e.g. via level-up plus an earlier re-learn) silently loses rows, and no test pins the intent.
findings.suggestion: Extract the version_group_details aggregation into a pure function and unit-test it with a fixture containing duplicate move entries across version groups.

findings.issue: compareRows encodes subtle contract points — nulls sort last in both directions (returns before the direction factor is applied), numeric vs localeCompare string sorting, and the level-then-name default ordering (lines 47-51) — none of which is tested beyond the single pikachu table the acceptance suite checks.
findings.suggestion: Move compareRows into a testable module and unit-test ascending/descending on each column type including null power/accuracy/PP, plus the aria-sort toggle behaviour.

findings.issue: Type-page moves are sorted by the humanized label rather than by API name as the spec's 'sorted alphabetically by name' suggests; localeCompare on hyphen-free labels can order differently than raw names, and no test pins the expected ordering.
findings.suggestion: Pick one key (label is probably fine), document it, and add a unit test asserting the order on the fire-type move list.

findings.issue: Non-404 API failures throw inside routeLoader$ with no fallback and no test; a 500/timeout from the API becomes an unhandled server error page rather than a graceful message.
findings.suggestion: Add an error-path unit test with a failing mock fetch and decide on a user-facing failure rendering.

summary: The agent wrote no tests at all: no runner, no script, no spec files in app/, leaving the data layer (api.ts), home-page filtering/pagination/URL state, and move-table sorting entirely dependent on the external acceptance suite. Worse, tracing the untested code surfaced at least one latent bug the suite misses — the popstate handler reads a stale location.url while filters use raw history.pushState — plus unverified rules like min-level dedup, nulls-last sorting, and permanent 404 caching. The pure helpers are trivially unit-testable and Qwik's recommended Vitest setup was one install away, so the omission is pure skipped effort.

untested.area: Data-layer mapping in cardsFromPokemonRefs (app/src/lib/api.ts:190-215): alternate-form exclusion (id > 10000), pokemon-to-species name resolution, hidden-ability flagging, dedup and dex-number ordering
untested.likelyBug: A refactor of the id/name extraction could silently include Mega forms, drop species, or link cards to /pokemon/<pokemon-name> instead of /pokemon/<species-name> — the acceptance suite covers a handful of species, so regressions on the long tail would ship unnoticed.

untested.area: Home page filtering, pagination and URL state (app/src/routes/index.tsx:52-60, 92-107): case-insensitive search on humanized names, 48-per-page slicing, page clamping, query-param omission, popstate sync
untested.likelyBug: Off-by-one in the slice bounds, page not reset on filter change, double-encoded params, or the stale location.url in the popstate handler (line 38) desyncing controls from the URL after back/forward.

untested.area: Move-table sorting contract (app/src/components/MoveTables.tsx:21-51): nulls last in both directions, aria-sort toggling, level-up default order by level then name
untested.likelyBug: Applying the direction factor before the null check would break missing-values-sort-last in descending order; breaking aria-sort or the two-click flip would also pass unnoticed outside the one pikachu table the acceptance suite inspects.

untested.area: latestFlavor and effect fallbacks (app/src/lib/api.ts:59-66, 236): last-English-entry selection, \s+ whitespace collapse, short_effect → flavor → '—' chain
untested.likelyBug: Taking the first English entry instead of the last, or dropping the trim/collapse, would render garbled or outdated descriptions with no failing test.

untested.area: Version-group aggregation and method ordering (app/src/lib/api.ts:299-360): min-level dedup, METHOD_ORDER tie-break sort, invalid ?game= fallback to the highest-order group
untested.likelyBug: Swapping min-level for first-seen, breaking the custom-vs-standard method sort tie-break, or accepting an unknown game param would produce subtly wrong move tables.

untested.area: HTTP caching and error handling (app/src/lib/api.ts:81-97): permanent null cache for 404s, thrown errors on non-404 failures
untested.likelyBug: A temporarily missing API resource stays not-found for the server lifetime, and a 500/timeout from the API becomes an unhandled routeLoader throw with no graceful page.

untested.area: Pure formatters (app/src/lib/format.ts:1-12): humanize, dexNumber zero-padding, displayNumber em dash
untested.likelyBug: A change to humanize's capitalization or padStart width would alter nearly every label on the site; cheap unit tests would catch it.

untested.area: Type-page moves list ordering (app/src/lib/api.ts:286-291): sorted by humanized label with localeCompare rather than by API name
untested.likelyBug: Ordering differences for hyphenated names relative to the spec's 'sorted alphabetically by name' would go unnoticed.
